titles: NIHR-HSPR-PA- Using participatory research to develop and implement a rural primary depression care model in India
descriptions:
This project involves the development and roll out of a care model for depression in a rural setting in India. To achieve this, the project uses a 'participatory' approach i.e., involving members of the rural community; the doctors, nurses and village-level health workers who deliver routine primary care services; and the district and state health department officials to discuss their perspectives and beliefs on how such a model should be (e.g., its components, modes of delivery, expectations out of the care received). The project aims to check if this model will be effective to identify persons with depression in the clinics, and improve their mental health outcomes.
This project is being implemented by Sangath, a mental health non-profit with 27 years of experience in India and twelve years of presence in the state of Madhya Pradesh in central India. 
A rural district in Madhya Pradesh has been selected for the project activities. Specifically, the depression care model will be implemented in nine primary care clinics with their catchment areas (villages), and nine other clinics will serve as the 'control group', which will receive routine health system support to deliver depression care. This will allow us to compare the effectiveness of the care model between these groups of clinics, on the percentage of people identified with depression, initiated on treatment, and those who improved their mental health outcomes (reduced depression severity) after receiving treatment. The project will be implemented from August 2025 to July 2028.
Nearly 50 million people live with depression in India. There are very few depression care models in India that have focused on adequate integration of depression care into rural primary care clinics, where most healthcare is delivered. Efforts so far have had limited engagement of the rural community, doctors and nurses, and local health systems, to identify local needs and perceptions towards such a care model. Developing and implementing a care model for depression by involving these stakeholders will ensure the model is adopted and used by the persons who are identified (or living) with depression, and potentially scaled up across the district to serve the rural population's mental health needs.

titles: To expand and nurture a collaborative network of leaders and change-makers working on governance, social justice and climate act
descriptions:

JST will (1) recruit at least 10 emerging leaders and change-makers (mid-career professionals aged 25-35) working on governance, social justice and/or climate action and (2) design and deliver a 6-month hybrid Fellowship Programme covering 10 countries of the Wider Europe and the Central Asia regions (building in sensitive cross-over points with network and parallel fellowship activities where appropriate). The programme will consist of (a) regular online programme of workshops, discussions and webinars covering core thematic content and practical skills for leading change and delivered by a combination of experienced network members and UK experts/practitioners from the public, civic and private sectors; (b) a 16-day residential programme in the UK providing first hand inspiration and insights into the values, ways of working and challenges faced by people and institutions in the UK and the approaches taken by different sectors to achieve fairer, more sustainable and inclusive societies; (c) individually-tailored programmes of meetings and placements with UK experts and counterparts to support the development and implementation of each Fellow’s individual action plan; (d) an online mentoring and support scheme drawing on the expertise and experience of senior John Smith Fellows across the EECA region.

After completing the initial Fellowship Programme, John Smith Fellows join a supportive and collaborative network of senior leaders and change-makers.

titles: Engagement of Global Creative Economy Council with government of the Kyrgyz Republic
descriptions: Creative Industries in Kyrgyzstan are at a crucial stage of convergence to effect meaningful changes and cultivate a conducive ecosystem for the creative economy's growth. The government of Kyrgyzstan, including the Ministry of Economy and Trade and the Administration of the President, acknowledge the significance of the creative economy and prioritize it in state policies. Consequently, fostering expertise and facilitating experience exchange among creative specialists becomes paramount. The project will fund a visit of experts from the Global Creative Economy Council (GCEC). GCEG members are world-leaders in their field who offer expert policy advice to government and mentoring to local creators. This interaction will not only enhance the knowledge base but also foster collaborations and innovation within the creative sector. It will create opportunities for skill development, market expansion, and the emergence of new ventures, ultimately contributing to economic diversification and sustainable development in Kyrgyzstan. The active involvement of both national and international stakeholders is essential to harness the full potential of the creative industries and drive positive socio-economic outcomes. The project will be implemented in cooperation with Ololo that will make their contribution by facilitating the visit and the event itself.

titles: Supporting medical service of the Border Service of State Committee for National Security of the Kyrgyz Republic
descriptions: The projects aims to develop and implement the tailored medical training (basic, intermediate and advanced) in line with international standards and their delivery to relevant EOD officers and medical personnel from the Border Service. In order to ensure sustainability of the provided assistance, the planned training events will be conducted in the form of Train of Trainers so that when the assistance is over, the border Service is able to continue the provision of the medical training on their own. In order to promote international standards in Kyrgyzstan, the provided trainings will be based on international standard - International Mine Action Standard (IMAS). Moreover, the planned training programme will be conducted on the basis of the Border Service Professional Development training Center in Osh, renovated and equipped by the POiB in 2023 as part of its efforts in increasing the training capabilities of the Border Service.

titles: From research and educating to action: Transforming energy policies to conserve the steppe eagles of Kazakhstan
descriptions: This project will employ the endangered Steppe Eagle - a flagship migratory species breeding primarily in Kazakhstan, to support conservation, awareness raising, research and improve Kazakhstan's energy power infrastructure to become more ecologically safe . The project will build positive engagement with key energy stakeholders from across the State and Private Sectors, enabling implementation of government policy and legislation that will bring benefits to both electricity infrastructure and biodiversity simultaneously, while building national capacity for scaling future remedial actions, and creating knowledge through novel educational materials across the country.

titles: IELTS for English language Teachers in the South of  Kyrgyzstan
descriptions:
Thirty public school and university teachers in the target areas of Osh City, Jalal-Abad City, and Kyzyl-Kiya in Batken region  will take an IELTS course provided by Kalpak Public Development Foundation (KPDF) partner, Kalpak English Academy (KEA). After finishing the course, beneficiaries will fly to Bishkek and take the official IELTS test, the cost of which is provided by the grant. 
Professors and public-school teachers often express the goal of passing IELTS to advance their careers, sometimes as a direct request from their superiors or the Ministry of Education. Furthermore, students often request their teachers to help them prepare for this exam. 

The overall duration of the course is 12 weeks. The course includes 2-week pre-IELTS training, 8 weeks of initial IELTS training, and 2 weeks of individual consultations, totaling more than 40 hours of study time.   

Upon completing the course, participants will be accommodated with plane flights, a per diem stipend, and will have IELTS licenses purchased for them to take the exam in Bishkek. At the final stage, an official award ceremony will be held in Osh.

The fund will help build capacity amongst Kazakh civil society to more effectively drive through necessary reform and support the Kazakh government in better delivering for its people. titles: Proactive steps to shield journalists
descriptions:
The project aims to mitigate the growing risks faced by independent media and journalists in Kyrgyzstan, especially in light of the increasingly restrictive legal environment. A key focus of the activities is enhancing the legal capacity of Kyrgyz media lawyers through targeted training workshops provided by Media Defense. These workshops will equip at least 10 lawyers, including five from MPI and five freelance lawyers, with the necessary skills to defend journalists facing legal action for their work.
The training will be conducted online and tailored to the specific needs of Kyrgyzstan media practitioners. A custom module covering European and international media legislation and how to navigate human rights mechanisms will be developed for this purpose. This module will also be available publicly on our Resource Hub, contributing to the improvement of the Russian-language information ecosystem. 
In addition to training, the project includes a study of how Kyrgyz media are impacted by restrictive laws, modeled after similar regulations in Russia. By conducting this research, the project aims to monitor the country's adherence to international obligations and provide evidence-based support for advocacy efforts aimed at protecting media freedom in Kyrgyzstan.

titles: Integrating the best practices of the UK Botanical Institutes in Tajikistan to encourage citizens to bond with nature.
descriptions:
The project plans to acquire knowledge and experience from the UK Botanical Institutes on the conservation of nature, by incorporating their approach and encouraging citizens to enjoy and respect nature. 

Output 1 of the project provides an opportunity for project partners to learn from the advanced practices by participating in the Study Exchange Visit to the UK Botanical Institutes. Priorities for the study exchange program will be nature conservation programs and events focused on involving citizens taking care of nature. 

In Output 2, three new gardens will be established within the Kulob Botanical Garden to attract and train different groups of citizens according to their interests and preferences, including the Children’s Garden, the Herbal and Medicinal Garden, the Landscaping and Home Plants Garden to increase participation of citizens in the conservation of nature. The priority for growing plant species within the established gardens will be given to endemic, rare, and endangered plant species.  

Output 3 covers awareness raising of citizens on available conservation programs for interested people during the Week of Open Doors in the Kulob Botanical Garden. The project achievements, including the results of the Nature Conservation Program, will be shared through mass media for the citizens of the Kulob area.

titles: Preventing and responding to cases of gender-based violence in Sughd, Tajikistan.
descriptions: This project will allow women victims of gender based violence and women at risk of violence to access support services, access legal support, and bring perpetrators of violence to justice. The provision of services acts as a deterrent to perpetrators of violence, who understand that there are organisations and people who are willing to defend the rights of women. Through social workers and psychologists, victims are able to receive support, and family counselling sessions are given, to help change attitudes towards the situation of women. With legal support, women are able to receive free of charge services to protect their rights and proceed with criminal convictions of the perpetrators when desired. These services have saved the lives of numerous women and have helped many more to rebuild their lives without violence. Local grassroots community leaders in 2 urban settings (Khujand) and 2 rural settings (J. Rasulov) will be trained to improve the effectiveness of their response to cases of violence against women, so that women are properly protected and can access help when they need it. Experience of working with community leaders has shown that improving the efficiency of their response has resulted in a reduction in the levels of violence in these communities.

titles: A scoping visit for peer engagement with the Union of Lawyers of the Republic of Tajikistan.
descriptions:
The aim is to strengthen peer engagement between the Law Society and the Union of Lawyers and identify opportunities for collaboration to promote good practice for legal professional bodies and support lawyers in Tajikistan.
This will be achieved through a scoping visit to Tajikistan to undertake a series of stakeholder meetings, including representatives of the Union of Lawyers, to document the mandate and functioning of the Union of Lawyers, examine good practice, and current challenges for lawyers. The findings will lead to recommendations for future collaboration to support the legal sector
As the professional body representing lawyers in Tajikistan, the Union of Lawyers has the remit to play a key role in promoting respect for rule of law and supporting lawyers as significant agents of the rule of law and equal access. By strengthening engagement between the Law Society  and the Union of Lawyers examining good practice for the independence of legal professional bodies in the region and recommending strategies to support the protection of legal professionals, this project will contribute to the realisation of sustainable development goal 16 and its focus on the promotion of the rule of law and access to 'justice at the national and international levels.

titles: Improving policy and practice of service delivery to people with disabilities
descriptions: The project aims to catalyse improvements to policy and practice in Kyrgyzstan by sharing experience from the UK on inclusion of people with disabilities. The project’s target beneficiaries are people with disabilities in Kyrgyzstan. This social group is more likely to be poor and economically excluded compared to the rest of the population.  The main government counterparts are the Kyrgyz ministries responsible for education and social policy and service delivery: the Ministry for Education and Ministry for Labour and Social Affairs. Other partners in delivery include schools and non-governmental organisations that play a direct role in the delivery of services to people with disabilities in the country. The project’s focus on UK-Kyrgyz partnerships, practical advice and policy change supports the UK’s long-term disability and inclusion goals in the country.

titles: Policing Violence Against Women and Girls: International Exchange Initiative
descriptions:
This project will build the knowledge and capability of police officers in Turkmenistan about different forms of VAWG, how to engage effectively with survivors of VAWG, and how to improve the policing of VAWG related crimes. Participants will be supported to develop action plans in order to use the lessons from shadowing to improve their home force’s policing of VAWG. The project will benefit women and girls in Turkmenistan, as well as participating police officers.

The Ending Violence team has been working with the UK National Police Chiefs Council (NPCC) on their approach to improving the policing of violence against women and girls (VAWG) in the UK.  As part of the process they are taking part in an exchange initiative with selected overseas police forces, including Turkmenistan, to share best practice.

The exchange will aim to share successes and lessons learned from the policing of VAWG in the UK; build relationships between forces pursuing similar aims; and improve the policing of VAWG in select overseas police forces.

descriptions: The project will enable 16 CSO leaders from all 14 regions and the Republic of Karakalpakstan to design and implement safe, lawful, rights-based campaigns with mentoring and small-grant support. Specifically, the training will focus on freedom of association with an emphasis on labour rights, delivered through a gender-inclusive approach and translated into community-level actions.

titles: Multiplying knowledge in the Kyrgyzstan: inclusive physical therapy for children with disabilities and needy families
descriptions: The project will improve the quality and accessibility of inclusive rehabilitation services for children with disabilities and their families in Kyrgyzstan by combining international experience, supervision, the work of regional Uplift center, and strengthening cooperation with government agencies.

titles: Strengthening the Kyrgyz creative sector
descriptions:
The project Strengthening the Kyrgyz creative sector  aims to strengthen the creative sector in Kyrgyzstan by completing and promoting a culturally significant film that highlights national heritage and empowers young professionals in the regions.
Through a series of structured activities - including final filming, post-production, and a national marketing and screening campaign - the project will create at least 10 temporary jobs, provide hands-on training for youth in filmmaking, and promote collaboration among regional talents. These activities will directly deliver outputs such as a completed feature film, a skilled creative team, and increased visibility of Kyrgyz culture through cinema.
By linking creative employment with cultural preservation, the project contributes to the broader goal of building a more inclusive and sustainable creative economy in southern Kyrgyzstan. Over the next few years, the trained professionals and established creative networks will continue to generate new audiovisual projects, ensuring long-term impact, stronger cultural identity, and expanded opportunities for young people in the creative industries

titles: Girls for Girls: Creative Mentorship Program
descriptions:
The project will launch the "Girls for Girls: Creative Mentorship Program," a structured, five-month initiative to create a professional pathway for 30 young women into Kyrgyzstan's creative economy. The project is structured in three phases. Activities begin with a 3-day "Creative Bootcamp" in Bishkek (Phase 1), which delivers foundational skills and matches participants with mentors. This is followed by a two-month tailored mentorship period (Phase 2), combining online guidance with project development. The project culminates in a public "Demo Day & Creative Fest" (Phase 3), where participants showcase their work to industry stakeholders.
The key Outputs will be a cohort of skilled young creatives, a portfolio of 15-20 youth-led projects, and a strengthened professional network. This will directly contribute to the project Purpose by fostering new talent. The longer-term impact will be the increased and sustained participation of women in Kyrgyzstan’s creative economy, leading to greater job creation and a more diverse, innovative cultural sector.

titles: Campus Circular Innovation Lab: Turning waste into worth

Through structured activities—including a baseline waste audit, installation of recycling tools, design workshops, and awareness events—the project will reduce campus waste streams while building student knowledge and leadership in circular economy practices.

titles: GEO: ZEG Tbilisi Storytelling Festival
descriptions: ZEG is a cross-disciplinary event that brings together storytellers from various professions, forces people out of their silos and into joint thinking about how we can collaboratively shape narratives for the future.  The inaugural edition took place in 2019, while the second edition was a one-day program titled ZEG in Focus: Ukraine, planned in response to the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022. In 2023 we hosted the first fully-fledged festival since 2019, with three days of ‘in-conversation’ sessions, panel discussions, networking events, workshops, and walking tours. For ZEG 2024 we plan to take the conversations started in 2023 to the next level with an even more diverse group of speakers which will bring together historians, musicians, chefs, actors, journalists, philosophers, comedians, educators, designers, activists, psychologists, medical practitioners, and tech industry leaders in one room to talk about the issues shaping the future. Notably, with 2024 being an important year for elections all over the world, including Georgia, we plan to organize several important sessions on this subject. This will include bringing several journalists and experts from other countries with scheduled elections to discuss challenges such as election rigging and the acute problem presented by election disinformation.

Monthly Summary: A comprehensive summary of developments from that month, presented in a video interview format on CivilNet. 

In-depth Articles: Commissioning in-depth articles to experts on democratic backsliding and democratic consolidation –– both theoretical and empirical, providing more detailed analysis and insights into specific topics. 

These reports will be presented on a dedicated page on CivilNet’s website, offering factual insights and incorporating commentary from experts. Through this monitoring and analysis, Democracy Watch aims to shed light on the challenges facing Armenia's democratic development and encourage informed dialogue to address them. At the end of each month, these reports will be summarized in a video interview format by one of the experts conducting and writing the analysis. 

Research will be conducted by the Regional Center for Democracy and Security and distributed on CivilNet platforms, including the website, Facebook and X (500K and  35K followers respectively), Youtube (265K subscribers), etc. CivilNet will also use its Newsletter (100K subscribers) to reach the target audiences.  

Topics will be chosen using an established methodology, based on existing scholarship on democratic backsliding, best practices of international watchdog organizations, and Armenian legislation, ensuring a systematic approach to monitoring and analysis.

titles: ARM: Strengthening UK-Armenia fashion ties in the framework of Yerevan Fashion Week (FDC)
descriptions: Support to the 2nd Yerevan Fashion Week (YFW) with the focus on promoting the Armenian textile and fashion industry in the international fashion scene, is a great opportunity to stimulate economic growth within Armenia’s fashion and textile industries, the sectors already predominantly driven by women and youth.

titles: AZN: Women’s Political Academy (Ulviyya Babasoy)
descriptions: The project aims to deliver trainings to 20 women aged 20-40 residing in Barda, Aghdam, Tartar, Yevlakh, Agjabedi, and neighbouring regions so that they can participate in the political arena; to raise awareness on the importance of women’s political engagement through motivational and educational activities; and to raise the profile of the Chevening programme by bringing the alumni together. This project will also contribute to the equal participation of people which is one of the core priorities of civil society organizations.

titles: AZN: Climate Policy Reform Initiative (BHRC)
descriptions: The Climate Policy Reform Initiative aims to enhance legal frameworks and policies for better climate resilience in Azerbaijan. By providing accessible legal aid and education online, the project seeks to empower citizens about their environmental rights and advocate for the integration of international climate standards into national laws. The initiative includes launching social media campaigns, producing educational videos, developing key policy documents, and organizing public discussions. Additionally, capacity-building workshops and training sessions will be conducted for volunteers and legal faculty students. The project targets reaching 500,000 individuals and aims to create a lasting impact on environmental advocacy and policy reform in Azerbaijan.

titles: AZE: Support Azerbaijan to develop Carbon Market (BSI)
descriptions:
The aim of the project is to support key stakeholders in Azerbaijan, the government and industry, to engage, inform and spark discussion on the main policies and tools to combat climate change and build the foundations for long term progress.
As part of its climate action, Azerbaijan is in the process of adopting carbon market legislation and possible tax incentives for greener companies. This will establish carbon compliance market that will control supply of carbon credits, regulate their trading, and incentivise companies to adopt a more sustainable business approach. 
Project activities will include:
1. Two (2) seminars, for 50-100 participants each, to raise awareness of carbon markets, carbon credit verification and UK carbon border adjustment mechanisms (CBAM) 
2. One-day roundtable discussion targeting policymakers, environmental policy, COP29 organisation committee, as well as business leaders, to highlight policy issues relevant to efforts to set foundations for carbon market infrastructure.  
3. 5-day training course

titles: BEL: Social care and dementia support to Jewish communities in Belarus (WJR)
descriptions:
World Jewish Relief has been working in Belarus since the 1990s in partnership with the local Belarusian organisation Hesed Rakhamim which supports over 2,000 older Jewish people in Minsk who require medical and social support.
The aim of this project is to improve the quality of life of older people living with dementia who are isolated from community life and lack specialist services. The project will also build support networks for those caring for a relative with dementia, increase awareness about dementia to build a more tolerant, dementia-friendly community. Lastly it aims to increase social contact for isolated people living alone by providing befriending services.

titles: BEL: Increasing the quality of care provided to children with severe disabilities (Belarussian Children’s Hospice)
descriptions: The project will improve the level of services provided by the CCH and strengthen its capacities, including the development of a volunteer network through cooperation with the Republican Volunteer Centre and student’s volunteer associations at universities. As well as building a dialogue with parents raising children with severe disabilities. The project plans to achieve three main outputs:Output 1. Strengthening the organizational capacity of the Charity Children’s Hospice (CCH) to improve the quality of social services provided to children with severe disabilitiesOutput 2. Enhancing the role of volunteers in protecting the rights of children with severe disabilities Output 3. Strengthening work with parents and parent communities to increasing their role in advocacy the rights of their children.

titles: GEO: Elections Monitoring
descriptions:
The Parliamentary elections planned in Georgia on 26th of October gains immense attention within as well as outside of the country. Therefore, the E day monitoring plays an important role in ensuring election taken place in fair and transparent way. By undertaking this initiative, the Embassy aims to contribute to the integrity of the electoral process.
The goal of this project is to ensure transparency, accountability, and public trust in the electoral process, as well as to provide actionable insights for improving future elections. Through active monitoring, the British Embassy will contribute to a more transparent electoral process, enhancing public confidence in the election results. The Embassy will produce a detailed report summarizing the electoral process, including any identified irregularities, which will be shared with the UK government and international stakeholders. By supporting Georgia's democratic institutions, the UK will reinforce its position as a key partner and ally in the region. The intelligence and data collected will enable the UK government to make more informed decisions regarding its future engagement with Georgia.

The latest democratic backsliding in Georgia has called for importance of ensuring all elections in Georgia are closely monitored for transparency. With this goal, BE Tbilisi elections observations team have joined other independent election observers in Georgia to monitor crucial parliamentary elections in 2024.

titles: BEL: Board game “[Belarus] Shtetl” (BJCH)
descriptions:
The project focuses on the development and creation of the board game [Belarus] Shtetl - a unique initiative with no current analogues in the realms of board games and education. It seamlessly integrates historical expertise, best practices in non-formal education, game design, artistic reinterpretation, and the contributions of experienced curators and producers. The game immerses players in the rich cultural tapestry of 19th-century Jewish shtetls in Belarus, offering an engaging blend of education, creativity, and entertainment.
The [Belarus] Shtetl board game project addresses the lack of awareness and visibility surrounding the rich cultural and historical heritage of Jews in Belarus - a history that has been intentionally marginalised and underrepresented in Belarusian education, culture and official public narratives for decades. Despite being an integral part of Belarusian history and global Jewish heritage, this topic mostly remains hidden. The absence of engaging and accessible educational tools further prevents younger generations from learning about this significant legacy, which is essential for understanding contemporary events, shaping modern identity, and appreciating a more accurate history.

titles: MOL: Enhance capacities of care workers to support children separated from their families (CCF)
descriptions: The project aims to support the implementation of 2022-2026 National Child Protection programme, through: 1) addressing a capacity gap in the social protection system, especially social workers’ capacities to conduct comprehensive children’ families’ and services’ assessment in the context of ensuring the right of every child to grow up in safe and nurturing family environment and following assessment to develop individual plans for children who are currently in Chisinau Institution for babies and young children (est. 20 children and their families) and 2) to enhance the skills and knowledge of 30 foster carers in 9 counties who look after over 98 children who lived through adverse childhood experiences. The priority will be offered to the foster families who have in placement children 2-7 years old. Foster carers will be supported to acquire and apply skills to enhance the relationship between children and adults as a strategy to understand and decrease the risks of conduct disorders, to reduce challenging behaviours and to promote and encourage positive behaviour. In addition, foster care managers from 9 counties will strengthen their knowledge of the CARE methodology for future monitoring. The foster parents and the specialists have been trained in a 6 hours training in 2024.

titles: GEO: Empowering Educators for a Green Future (GREDA)
descriptions: The proposed project aims to implement an educational program in collaboration between the British Embassy and Georgian Renewable Energy Development Association, targeting teachers across Georgia to enhance their knowledge of renewable energy and environmental protection. Building on Georgian Renewable Energy Development Association's 2022 project experience, which educated over 1,000 high school students with USAID support, this initiative seeks to empower educators with accurate and comprehensive knowledge. The program will involve workshops in 10 Georgian regions, focusing on civics and geography teachers who directly engage with youth.

titles: GEO: Design Youth Livelihood: Create and Employ (SAORSA)
descriptions: The project aims to support the development of professional orientation and career development system for the effective employment in the Adjara region. The main objective of the project is to increase the competitiveness of young people through strengthening self-esteem, labour market orientation, job search and self-presentation skills; and to promote operational and effective communication between employers and job seekers, supporting vocational and higher education institutions. Within the framework of the project, young people aged 18-29 living in the Adjara region will undergo a training program consisting of three main modules: career development and employment skills, financial literacy and entrepreneurship. Within the framework of the training program, young people will receive new knowledge, acquire employment skills and develop personal and professional values, which will ensure the improvement of their financial awareness, employment opportunities and economic independence.

titles: GEO: Empower Inclusion: Combating Gender and Disability Disinformation in Georgia (Alliance of Women With disability)
descriptions:
The Anti-Gender Disinformation (GID) Project in Georgia addresses the harmful impact of disinformation on gender equality and marginalized groups, including women, youth, and individuals with disabilities. Through targeted activities, the project seeks to raise awareness, promote positive narratives, and empower communities to combat disinformation effectively. 
This project plans to use two days workshops with the goal to find more supporters and empower the stakeholders. The target groups for the workshops are: disability community, CSOs and civic activists. The goal of those workshops are not just raise awareness about GID, but empower the community.

titles: GEO: Contest - My Heritage (National Trust of Georgia)
descriptions: One of the main functions of the National Trust of Georgia at this point in the country’s evolution, has turned out to be awareness-raising. There is an unusually low knowledge and awareness of the abilities and techniques of restoration, recycling, and valuation of historic properties in Georgia – compared to most of Europe. These locally popular, well publicised heritage events spread the word particularly well into the general population. The National Trust of Georgia Heritage Awards are presented to individuals who have shown imagination and commitment to heritage preservation, either with their own properties or in the heritage sector in general. The point is not only to reward local people, but generate wide publicity in the field of cultural restoration, encouraging imaginative repurposing of buildings and ecological reuse, rather than demolition. Both previous projects have generated wide and favourable press coverage locally and nationally.

titles: ARM: Vehicle-Based Mobile Laboratory to Enhance Air Quality Monitoring (UNDP)
descriptions:
Air pollution in Armenia, particularly in Yerevan, is a significant concern  for Government, citizens and environmental groups. Recognizing this, the Environment Agency Austria, within the UNDP-implemented EU4Climate project, conducted a needs assessment of Armenia’s ambient air monitoring system and provided recommendations for improvement. 
These recommendations became a discussion topic at the high-level policy dialogue “GREEEN Platform” meeting, chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister Khachatryan on 16 June 2023, following which, the Government allocated funds for two new air quality monitoring stations in Yerevan. Additionally, the Government of Japan committed to equip three additional observation stations for automatic measuring atmospheric air pollutants. These stations will enable the measurement of key air pollutants, including particular matters such as dust particles (PM2.5 and PM10), nitrogen and sulfur dioxide, carbon monoxide and ground-level ozone. It will also allow real-time data collection, which will be made publicly available and facilitate the calibration of widely used air quality sensors, including those installed at construction sites.
The “Hydrometeorology and Monitoring Center” state non-commercial organization (HMC), is mandated to systematically monitor environmental conditions, including air quality. Given the ongoing efforts for expansion and modernization of Armenia's atmospheric air quality monitoring system, ensuring the continuous and accurate operation of these monitoring stations is crucial. This requires constant control, diagnostics, calibration and maintenance that are essential for ensuring the accuracy of air quality data. This can be ensured through mobile services. 
A vehicle-based mobile laboratory will allow these processes to be carried out directly at the monitoring stations, preventing data gaps and increasing the reliability of the air quality measurements.

titles: MOL: International Women Judges Day and Cash Smuggling
descriptions:
The event is a half day conference followed by an evening reception. 
The event is a half day conference followed by an evening reception. In the afternoon there will be two sessions. The first will be delivered by the SOCnet regional coordinator for the CEN region and a female UK Judge, in which they will deliver a presentation on an ongoing cash smuggling project being delivered in the region. It will outline the challenges of cash smuggling identified in each country, the approach taken and progress made to date. The second session will be a panel event consisting of senior female judges and members of the criminal justice system in Moldova, the UK and Romania, discussing the role of women in the justice sector specialising in economic crime. The afternoon event will be attended by up to 30 prosecutors and judges from all regions of Moldova and members of the criminal justice community generally. The evening reception will mark International Women Judges Day and a senior female Judge from the UK shall deliver an inspirational speech. There will be up to 60 attendees, with additional guests from the National Institute of Justice, Ministries of Justice and Interior and international partners.

titles: GEO: Tbilisi School of Political Studies (TSPS) – September Seminar
descriptions:
The Tbilisi School of Political Studies (TSPS) is a leading NGO dedicated to training young professionals and civil servants in democratic governance. In Georgia, this entails fostering dialogue on key issues such as democratic transformation, free and fair elections, institutional strengthening, decentralisation, civic engagement, and the development of a resilient civil society.  The TSPS autumn seminar will bring together experts drawn from the fields of academia, civil society, journalists and the diplomatic community, to discuss challenges and identify potential solutions relating to democratic backsliding and Georgia’s turning away from the Euro-Atlantic pathway.
  
UK support for this event will allow us to support work to bring together thought leaders working in diverse fields, to discuss the challenges currently facing Georgia and identify a way forward.  It will allow the British Embassy Tbilisi to deepen our engagement with experts working in the fields of democracy and governance, influence partners’ approaches, and demonstrate UK thought leadership.  As a result of the conference, we will identify practical steps we take take in coordination with partners to protect democratic space and counter authoritarian trends in Georgia.

titles: ARM: Democracy Watch 2.0: Empowering Civic Resilience in Armenia (Civiltas)
descriptions:
Democracy Watch 2.0 is a joint initiative by CivilNet and the Regional Center for Democracy and Security aimed at strengthening democratic resilience in Armenia ahead of the pivotal 2026 parliamentary elections. Building on its successful first phase, the project will deliver high-quality, non-partisan analysis of Armenia’s democratic trajectory, addressing emerging risks such as government overreach, media politicization, and potential external interference.

The goal of the project is to strengthen democratic resilience and civic awareness in Armenia.

titles: MOL: Stronger Services, Better chances (CCF)
descriptions:
Stronger Services, Better Chances addresses a key gap in Moldova’s Child Care Reform: the limited capacity of foster care services to respond to children with complex social and psychological needs. Many foster carers and specialists are not yet equipped to support children with conduct disorders, often linked to Adverse Childhood Experiences. Building on the 2024–2025 FCDO-funded initiative, the project will train 70 foster care specialists nationwide and mentor professionals in 8 counties on CARE (Child-Adult Relationship Enhancement) positive parenting programme. In addition, 52 foster carers will receive training—either as first-time participants or through refresher sessions—and all will benefit from tailored in-person mentoring and follow-up support. Alongside capacity building, the project will advance policy dialogue, drawing on Moldova’s endorsement of the Global Charter on Child Care. A multi-stakeholder roundtable will set priorities for extending the 2022–2026 National Child Protection Programme beyond 2026. By combining training, mentoring, and advocacy, the project strengthens foster care services and improves outcomes for children.
This project will give foster carers and specialists the tools and confidence to better support children with complex needs, helping them grow in safe and nurturing families. By strengthening services and shaping stronger child protection policies, it creates better chances for children in Moldova to thrive.

titles: GEO: Understanding Heritage: Regional activities (NTG)
descriptions:
To address the gap in the education system, the National Trust of Georgia (NTG) is launching a creative and inclusive educational initiative aimed at raising awareness about the significance of heritage and environmental conservation among children and youth in Tbilisi and selected regions, Kvemo Kartli and Imereti.
Overall, the project promotes democratic change, social development, and a deeper understanding of environmental and cultural heritage, thereby supporting sustainable development.

titles: BEL: Development of home-based palliative care for young adults in the regions (BCH)
descriptions:
The project will improve the quality of palliative home care provided to young adults with palliative status. And, as a result, it’ll improve their quality of life by increasing the level of competence of helping professionals in state social protection institutions (territorial centers for social services) and clinics as well as guardians (including parents) of young adults with palliative status in Mogilev and the Mogilev region.
As part of the project, specialists from the Charitable Children's Hospice (??H) will conduct approximately 10 training sessions at regional social service centres (RSSC) for social workers, carers, medical staff, other specialists in this field and for guardians/parents of young adults. The topics of the training sessions will include general information about palliative care, home care aspects, technical aids for social rehabilitation, communication, psychological and spiritual aspects of palliative care.

titles: BEL: Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM): migrants in vulnerable situations and refugees in Belarus (IOM)
descriptions:
IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) is a robust field-tested data collection and analysis system that produces critical multi-layered information on migrant profiles, routes, drivers, vulnerabilities, and intentions to enable decision makers and responders provide context specific and effective programmes and policies. DTM will be tasked with the collection of primary data and analysis to generate insights, on the needs, vulnerabilities, intentions and protection challenges of migrants in vulnerable situations and refugees in Belarus. 
Through this intervention, IOM will customize DTM tools and methodologies to the context in Belarus. Taking in account limited official data to inform the data needs of UN agencies to respond to the situation, DTM will provide information on the location, profile, routes, needs and intentions of migrants and refugees. For governmental stakeholders, DTM will enable evidence-based data on profiles of refugees and migrants present in the country.

titles: GEO: Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Education in Georgia (ISET PI)
descriptions: The project seeks to organize a full-day international conference in Tbilisi on “AI in Education: Advancing Benefits in Teaching and Learning in Georgia’s Universities”, engaging Georgian academics, university administrators, and students in knowledge exchange on AI applications in teaching and learning. The event will feature both local and international speakers, who will share best practices, innovations, benefits, risks, and emerging trends in AI adoption. Prior to the conference, the project team will conduct a desk review of global practices and an online survey of Georgian universities to identify current AI applications, challenges, and knowledge gaps. These findings will inform the conference agenda, ensuring sessions address the specific needs and interests of Georgian higher education institutions.

titles: GEO: DataFest Tbilisi – Conference Costs (ForSet)
descriptions:
DataFest Tbilisi is the largest annual data and AI event in Eastern Europe and the South Caucasus, gathering over 1,000 participants from business, technology, media, academia, and civil society. This project will support the participation of leading British AI and data experts at DataFest Tbilisi 2025 to strengthen professional connections between the UK and Georgian AI communities.
Through keynotes, panels, and workshops, British speakers will share best practices in artificial intelligence, data science, and responsible innovation, fostering direct knowledge transfer and collaboration. Structured networking activities will help establish long-term partnerships, mentorships, and joint initiatives between UK and Georgian professionals.

titles: BEL: Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration for Migrants Stranded on the Territory of Belarus (IOM)
descriptions: IOM will render Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration (AVRR) services to the most vulnerable migrants stranded in Belarus who wish to return home and against whom no criminal proceedings have been instituted, nor has a decision been taken on forced deportation, unless such a decision is revoked. All returns will be implemented strictly following the IOM Guidance Notes and Standard Operating Procedures, and applicable international law, including the principle of non-refoulement, rights-based and protection-sensitive approach, best interests of the child, and coordinated with the IOM office in each country of origin well in advance. IOM will facilitate voluntary return to countries where conditions for return are met based on the IOM Voluntary Returns Suspension and Pre-Return Clearances List.

titles: GEO: Green Future: Renewable Energy Awareness for Georgian Youth (GREDA)
descriptions:
GREDA will deliver an engaging climate and renewable energy education programme for students aged 14–18 across 10 Georgian regions with strong renewable potential. Working with the Ministry of Education and regional Resource Centres, GREDA will run school-based seminars that combine age-appropriate content, hands-on activities, and mini-quizzes to select regional teams. The programme culminates in a national ‘What? Where? When?’ style quiz final in Tbilisi, motivating students from the regions to excel and providing strong public visibility.

The project advances UK objectives on climate action, inclusive education and youth empowerment, and UK–Georgia cooperation in the green transition. It delivers measurable outcomes (students reached, knowledge gains, regional coverage) within a 5-month window at good value by leveraging GREDA’s existing materials and regional networks while ensuring safeguarding for minors.

titles: ADF14 Promissory Notes
descriptions: This is the UK’s 13th replenishment to the concessional arm of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to fund concessional support to its poorest member countries to 2028. The ADB provides loans to wealthier developing members, and concessional loans or grants to its poorer members via the fund. The Business Case notes ADF 14 envisages a substantial uplift from $4 billion to $5 billion (though roughly constant – 1% up - in real terms), with the ADB itself funding half the increase and nearly half (47%) of the overall total, “a historic high”1. It states that key foci of this replenishment round are to increase the level of transfer from ABD’s net income, a stronger ($1.3 bn) offer for the Pacific small island developing states (SIDS), a new ‘community window’ of $1.15bn in offers for Afghanistan ($815m), Myanmar ($200m), and Rohingya refugees ($100m)2 and increased focus on climate and gender impacts ($437m for adaptation and $194m for gender).

titles: Securing Access for Field Engagement in Humanitarian Hubs - SAFE Hubs
descriptions: Providing support for the security of humanitarian hubs in North East Nigeria through UNDSS services

titles: Programme funded Behavior change and advocacy (FA and TA),
descriptions: General the post is aims to provide technical support to the Ministry ; specifically aims to support the Ministry of Education to protect education gains to date, and level up regions with poor education outcomes, through a focus on equity, including girls, other marginalized groups and developing regions.

titles: Design component for SEMESTA
descriptions: This component is to effectively design the SEMESTA Programme. Through this component, the programme team will: (i) design a programme that aligns with the overarching FCDO's ODA strategy and goals; (ii) plan to optimise the use of resources while ensuring the funds available are allocated efficiently and effectively; (iii) identify potential risks and develop strategies to mitigate them; (iv) plan mechanisms for monitoring and evaluation that are essential to track progress; (v) correctly set the long-term outcomes and impacts of the programme.

titles: Forest, Agriculture and Sustainable Trade (FAST)
descriptions: FAST aims to accelerate palm oil and cocoa actors (including the government and industries) to demonstrate sustainable and responsible business practices while protecting the environment and alleviating poverty. The project will also increase the readiness and adoption of certification programs that ensure sustainable practices which can provide frameworks for responsible sourcing and production, and lesson learned from timber experience to other commodities.

titles: SEMESTA Programme Management
descriptions: This component is to support the delivery of SEMESTA Programme ie. the Forest, Agriculture and Sustainable Trade (FAST) component and the Critical Minerals Management for Sustainability (MAKMUR) component. This component will provide a crucial role in ensuring the programme is effectively and efficiently implemented and monitored, to maintain accountability and transparency of the use of ODA fund channelled through the SEMESTA programme.

titles: Critical Minerals Management for Sustainability (MAKMUR)
descriptions:
Build the capacity and political support required to implement policies, regulations and voluntary actions for a resilient and sustainable critical minerals supply chain in Indonesia, while enhancing domestic value addition and benefits from mineral production and battery and EV supply chains.

The focus areas are: 
- The critical minerals supply chain (with a focus on nickel), including governance and regulatory challenges and ESG risks.
- Sustainable mining practices, decarbonization, mining standards compliance.
- The impact of captive coal use in nickel processing.
- Downstream policies to increase domestic added value through responsible development of manufacturing capacity in EV and battery production

titles: Support for the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme
descriptions: Funding for the coordinator of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS) as part of pre-employment screening efforts to reduce perpetrators moving between organisations.

titles: Harmonisation of SEAH data collection and reporting
descriptions: Harmonisation of SEAH data collection and reporting to increase transparency and understanding of data trends across the HDP sector.

titles: Humanitarian Quality Assurance Initiative (HQAI)
descriptions: The Humanitarian Quality Assurance Initiative (HQAI) certifies organisations against the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS), helps build good practice, transparency and accountability across the sector, including a Facilitation Fund that helps national and local organisations to access support to meet the standard.

titles: Private Sector Safeguarding Support (SLN)
descriptions: Support to the coordinator of the Safeguarding Leads Network (SLN), to lead coordination of improved safeguarding practices across the private sector.

titles: Approaches to raise Safeguarding Standards
descriptions: Approaches to raise safeguarding standards across the sector to increase capacity and capability. Providing a basis for more coherent and collective action and to act as an anchor for multistakeholder dialogue and best practice on PSEAH approaches, challenges and resourcing.

titles: The Common Approach to Protection from SEAH
descriptions: A new online guide and tool to help all people and organisations working in Humanitarian Development and Peace settings take action to protect people from SEAH. CAPSEAH brings actions from existing practice, policies and standards together to provide a basis for more coherent and collective action and to act as an anchor and repository for multistakeholder dialogue and best practice on PSEAH approaches, challenges and resourcing.

titles: Support to PSEA-CAP co-ordinators
descriptions: Providing support to OCHA PSEA Coordinators in the highest risk countries to reduce the risk of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and sexual harassment.

titles: CAPSEAH Safeguarding and Accountability Fund
descriptions:
Fund with the aim of promoting a safer and more accountable aid system through,
1. SEAH trends and PSEAH progress is measured and analysed enabling evidence informed prevention and response. 
2. Organisations are better able to prevent and respond SEAH with innovative solutions that meet evidence informed needs.
3. Global public goods support accountability, prevention and response across the sector

titles: Investigator Qualification Training Scheme (IQTS)
descriptions: The Investigator Qualification Training Scheme (IQTS) strengthens investigative practices to improve responses to SEAH violations, ensure accountability, and prevent future harm. Grounded in CHS Alliance’s survivor-centred investigation guidance, the programme focuses on three key areas: promoting survivor centred SEAH investigations, expanding investigator capacity (supported by Humentum), and ensuring access to trained professionals.

titles: UNAIDS Core Support 2024-7
descriptions: Core funding to the Joint UN Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) for 2024-7 in support of the Global AIDS Strategy and Sustainable Development Goal 3.

titles: The Safeguarding Resource and Support Hub 2
descriptions: This project aims to build capability of organisations who deliver international aid to strengthen their safeguarding policies and practices against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEAH).

titles: Safeguarding Resource and Support Hub Programme: Evaluation
descriptions: The aim of the project is to evaluate the performance of the RSH programme to date,  to determine how far the RSH programme has achieved expected results, analyse the value for money of the programme and capture key lessons and learning. The output will be used to inform future FCDO programming in relation to safeguarding against SEAH, and wider capability building.

titles: HQAI Facilitation Fund
descriptions:
Facilitation Fund will enable the development of its three core activities:
• Grant subsidies to L/NNGOs: Subsidies are granted for a three-year period (50 to 90% of the audit
costs are subsided depending on several factors).
• Audit groups of L/NNGOS: Group audit approaches allow for several independent organisations to
join forces in a) implementing the CHS, b) learning and improving together and c) being
independently assessed (economies of scale).
• Develop a network of local auditors and audit facilitators: The creation of a pool of local experts will
contribute to the creation of auditing capacities closer to the sites of operations of HQAI partners.

titles: Interagency Protection against Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Community Outreach and Communication Fund
descriptions:
The Interagency PSEA Community Outreach & Communication Fund is a multi-donor, interagency grant mechanism 
established by UNHCR and the International Council of Voluntary Agencies (ICVA). titles: EITI Subscription Payment
descriptions: The Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) is a global initiative that promotes the open and accountable management of oil, gas and mineral resources. Under this programme, the UK will make its annual subscription to the EITI. EITI is active in 57 countries and is an influential voice with governments in much of the developing world. It is designed to improve accountability and public trust for the revenues paid and received for a country’s natural resource extraction, including critical minerals. This is a major concern in many resource-rich developing nations where the benefits of resource extraction are lost through mismanagement and corruption. Adherence to EITI principles helps ensure that developing countries benefit from a higher percentage of revenue from natural resource extraction and encourages the establishment and maintenance of robust governance systems, which aid stable investment climates.

The UK is joining a broad coalition of partners to contribute financially and technically to this initiative, which supports inclusive and equitable care systems. These systems have the potential to benefit women and girls in all their diversity, free up their time, and create low-carbon, decent jobs. The initiative works with multiple stakeholders, including UN agencies, national and local governments, civil society, unions, academia, the private sector, and the media, to promote a whole-of-society approach to care. This partnership forms part of the Jobs and Inclusive Growth Centre of Expertise which will also leverage the knowledge and expert advice of the initiative to inform other components of the COE.

titles: Partnerships for Growth: Women Entrepreneurs Finance (We-Fi) Initiative - Scaling the Care Economy

By providing blended finance, technical assistance, and market access through multilateral development bank partners, the Care Call aims to reduce unpaid care burdens, increase women’s economic participation, and create decent jobs, unlocking opportunities across childcare, eldercare, health, and digital care services. This effort not only strengthens care systems but also accelerates gender equality and economic resilience in developing countries. This partnership forms part of the Jobs and Inclusive Growth Centre of Expertise which will also leverage the knowledge and expert advice of the initiative to inform other components of the COE.

titles: IBRD Hybrid Capital contribution
descriptions: The UK will make a £100m (c.$127m) hybrid capital contribution to the World Bank’s IBRD. This will unlock £800m in extra lending from the IBRD for Middle Income Countries (MICs). This extra financing will be used for projects that will (1) help MICs achieve the Sustainable Development Goals and reduce poverty and (2) tackle global challenges, such as climate mitigation and pandemic preparedness. Hybrid Capital is a new financing instrument for the World Bank, allowing countries to voluntarily increase their subscribed capital / funding to the IBRD without the need for wider funding round by all countries. It does not carry the same rights / privileges as capital through a routine IBRD capital increase. It is not a ‘core contribution’ to the World Bank, therefore, though the UK could convert its Hybrid Capital into a core contribution as part of a future IBRD funding round.

titles: Strengthening Ukraine's Social Protection Systems and Services for a Child-Centred Recovery
descriptions:
SPIRIT aims to enhance the capacity of Ukraine’s social protection system to better meet the needs of the most vulnerable with more inclusive, effective, and resilient social protection programmes.

Under Outcome 1 (National), this will be achieved through the establishment of a Project Management Unit (PMU) for reforms; coordination, evidence generation and advocacy activities; and operational pilots. Overall, Outcome 1 will include support to establish the foundations for evidenced-based reform and improved coordination across the Government of Ukraine, International Financial Institutions (IFIs) and key development actors in line with the Ukraine plan and broader sector priorities. This may include support to accompany key reforms in the areas of social protection benefits and services, social inclusion and capacity coordination.

Under Outcome 2 (Local), a small-scale grants (SSG) mechanism will be established to support the most vulnerable families with children and to mitigate the risk of child separation from caregivers in Better Care priority Oblasts, notably Volyn, Kharkiv, Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Zakarpattia, Lviv, Khmelnytskyi, Poltava, Dnipro, and Chernivtsi regions. The potential of different types of social service providers will be activated through the SSG Initiative established in partnership with the MoSP of Ukraine and National Fund for Social Protection of Persons with Disabilities, which serves as the Ministry’s ‘Purchasing Agency’. This will be achieved through the provision of support to, at least, 100 community-based social service providers/civil society organizations through the provision of grants and capacity building in the target regions, in order to both improve access of at least 10,000 families with children to community-based social services whilst also building local marketplaces of social service providers.

titles: Celebrating 16-days of activism against gender-based violence in Katutura and Okahandja.
descriptions:
The aim of the project is to celebrate the 16-days of activism against Gender-Based Violence in three communities, in order to encourage community members to reflect on the issue and ensure they know (in particular girls and women) who to contact should they face violence at home. 
Key beneficiaries will be 2,400 community members from two areas in Katutura, Windhoek and one area in the main location of Okahandja, of which 60% (1,560) are women and girls. 
Through interactive activities with the community dance troupe, our photo exhibition ‘the caring Namibian man’, clips and films, the audience will be encouraged to reflect on what happens in their location, share ideas on how they can become agents for change, ensure there’s zero tolerance for gender-based violence in their area and commit to do better during this festive season.

Ultimately, the initiative aims to promote a more inclusive and resilient democratic system in Namibia by promoting informed civic activism and facilitating greater youth involvement in political decision-making. descriptions: This project will support the Country Business Plan’s objective of empowering women and girls, particularly those with disabilities, through promoting inclusive education and better access to adequate educational materials.

titles: Support for Climate Resilient cash Transfers in Malawi through Give Directly
descriptions: The project will target the most climate vulnerable communities in Malawi to enable households facing extreme weather and other negative income shocks mitigate the associated shocks hence avoiding poverty traps.

titles: Fostering Indonesia’s Sustainable Digital Health Innovations through Regulatory Sandbox Implementation
descriptions:
The project is to provide technical assistant to the Ministry of Health to implement the regulatory sandbox related to other digital health innovations clusters. The regulatory sandbox is aimed to foster new digital health innovations and is expected to implement in 2024-2025.

The proposed project includes the following activities:
1. Prioritisation of digital health innovation clusters for upcoming regulatory sandboxes
2. Implementation of a continued and sustainable regulatory sandbox Batch 2
3. Supporting the supervision and nurturing process of digital health innovators enrolled in the regulatory sandbox (Batch 1)

titles: Gap Analysis for Health Genomics Ecosystem in Indonesia
descriptions:
The project seeks to understand the existing gaps in the current Indonesia national genomics initiatives and benchmark against global best practices, standards and regulations in the genomics space including the following scopes:
- Comparison with other international jurisdictions
- Benchmarking BGSi’s genomic services with international standards using levers and sub-levers, and with focus on policy/regulation and operational aspects
- Determining current gaps in Indonesia’s genomics ecosystem and best practices in implementing national genomics initiatives
- To provide recommendations on action plan to align with global best practices.

The anticipated outcomes of these projects aim to bolster the genomics landscape and its associated parties in Indonesia. This will be achieved by pinpointing existing gaps and determining actionable steps that can be taken to advance genomic efforts within the nation.

descriptions: This is for interpreter and translation services for project on Indonesia Digital Health and Workforce Development with NHS Consortium for Global Health. The interpreters are highly required for year 2 activities that will include Communities of Practice for different categories of stroke care professions and policymakers, Actions Learning Sets, and adaptation of Fundamentals of Acute Care and Treatment after Stroke (FACTS) e-module. The participants from all these activities are all Indonesian healthcare workforce, from doctors, nurses, therapists, and policy makers.

titles: Programme-Funded Staff for Indonesia Digital Health Programme
descriptions:
Payment for programme-funded staff based in British Embassy Jakarta (Health Adviser and Head of Health Team, SEO). 

This is to improve the capacity of Digital Health Programme team to deliver the programme.

titles: Regulatory Framework System for Health Regulation
descriptions: The project aims to support the Ministry of Health to streamline and harmonise the management of health regulations, ensuring adherence to Law No. 17 of 2023.It will be conducted through several phases:Phase 1: Proof of Concept Phase, which entails consolidation and categorisation of existing health regulations, identifying inconsistencies and gaps; Phase 2: Regulatory Database & Advance Search Phase, consisting creation of a comprehensive database with an advanced search function for efficient retrieval of relevant regulations;Phase 3: Regulatory Framework System Phase, which will develop an actual system by perpetual licence to use; and Phase 4: Capacity Building Phase to disseminate knowledge for National health Policy Agency (BKPK) Ministry of Health personnel on system utilisation.

titles:
Shaping the Future of Indonesia’s Healthcare through the Digital Health Transformation
Strategy (DHTS) 2025-2029
Shaping the Future of Indonesia’s Healthcare through the Digital Health Transformation  Strategy (DHTS) 2025-2027
descriptions: The project is aimed at supporting the Ministry of Health in the development of Digital Health Transformation Strategy (2025-2029) and its implementation roadmap. This project will cover two out of four missions including 1) ensuring inclusive, efficient, and use-oriented digitalization of health services; and 2) encouraging innovation and collaboration in the digital health ecosystem. These all will ensure Indonesia to build a sustainable, data-driven, and inclusive digital health ecosystem with a clear strategy and actionable actions to achieve the ambition.

titles: Indonesia Digital Health and Workforce Development
descriptions:
This project is arranged under Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with National Health Services England (NHS England) to provide flexible, strategic and technical health expertise to the Government of Indonesia for digital health and workforce planning. The subject matter experts are derived from NHSC Member organisations, through the NHS Consortium Technical Advisory Service (CTAS). 

The project covers from period of 1 April 2023 to 31 March 2025, but this AMP will only cover remaining activities starting from August 2024 to March 2025. 

The workforce mainstream is mainly related on workforce planning and stroke care workforce collaboration. The stroke care workforce has entered its Year 2 of implementation, focusing on stroke care service design, workforce, training and education in Indonesia. The main stakeholders are the Ministry of Health and Rumah Sakit Pusat Otak Nasional.

titles: Midwifery Capacity Advancement for Equitable Sexual and Reproductive Health and Reproductive Rights (MARCH) Project
descriptions:
The funding is for UNFPA to provide technical assistance on three interconnected pillars of midwifery capacity advancement for sexual and reproductive health and rights: regulatory frameworks, midwifery education, and continuing professional development. 

This project is aimed at improving national capacities to implement a regulatory framework that enhances the quality of midwifery workforce with the following outcomes. 
the following outcomes. 
1. Regulatory framework at the national level effectively provides a national strategy for continuing professional development of the midwifery workforce
Under this outcome, the project will develop policy recommendations, a a National Midwifery Continuing Professional Development (CPD) Framework, and a CPD pilot programme to improve the quality of midwifery services. 
2. Midwifery education stakeholders are enhanced through the implementation of midwifery education that is aligned to International Confederation of Midwives (ICM) standards.
Under this outcome, the project will improve the accreditation standards for midwifery education aligned with the ICM through some stages from baseline assessment of the current accreditation to piloting the upgraded accreditations in selected midwifery institutions (health polytechnics). It will then train the midwifery teachers with updated teaching methodologies and resources based on the new curricula. 
3. Midwifery Continuing Professional Development (CPD) programmes are strengthened in producing empowered and competent health workers who are capable of providing quality reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health services.
Under this outcome, the project will build professional capacity of in-service midwifery, as well as other skills such as conducting research/study on midwifery-led Care (MLC).

titles: Genomics and Science Dojo: Accelerating Outputs and Action 2.0 and UK-Indonesia Genomic Forum 2025
descriptions:
Genomics and Science Dojo 2.0 aims to build on the Dojo 1.0 to further enhance biomedical science and genomic analysis skills for improved decision-making, dissemination and publication. Capacity for genomic data analysis and inference is crucial to provide evidence-based policy for use of genomics to promote health and development.

The outcomes will be indicated from the following: 
(1)Improvement in technical skills of researchers and academia on genomics data analysis. This will be measured by the proportion of participants with an improvement of knowledge by 80%.
(2)Improvement in soft skills of researchers and academia to showcase the genomics analysis results through written or verbal format. This will be indicated by the number of publications/knowledge products resulting from this project and qualified to be published or showcase/presented at a scientific conference or wider audience.
(3)Enhancement genomics dojo implementation for wider audience. The curriculum and workbook will be made available for a wider user and scale up. The number of participants from clinicians (externals/visitors) will also be measured to assess the success.

The UK-Indonesia Genomic Forum aims to build capacity, strengthen UK-Indonesia partnerships in health genomics, supporting policy development, research, and industry collaborations that benefits populations in both the UK and Indonesia, and accelerating research, innovation, and translation into public health improvements. The Forum aligns with the Dojo target and will help to connect the Dojo participant with the UK stakeholders in the Forum.

titles: Refining and Assisting Digital Health Transformation Strategy (DHTS 2025-2029) Implementation
descriptions:
The project with AMANA aims to provide technical assistance in advancing the Digital Health Transformation Strategy (DHTS) 2025–2029, by translating the strategic document into a tangible and measurable five-year implementation roadmap. This roadmap will serve as a practical guide to ensure the effective execution of the strategy. 

The overarching goal of the project is to support the successful implementation of digital health transformation in Indonesia by enhancing stakeholder readiness through three key activities: 
- Refinement of the Digital Health Transformation Strategy (2025–2029) 
- Development of the DHTS Implementation Roadmap 
- Stakeholder Capacity Building and Technical Support for Roadmap Implementation 

The Digital Health Transformation Strategy (DHTS) 2025–2029 and its accompanying roadmap are not standalone documents. They serve as strategic policy instruments aligned with broader national development goals. Specifically, they support the Ministry of Health’s agenda as outlined in the Health Sector Master Plan (Rencana Induk Bidang Kesehatan [RIBK]) 2025–2029, the National Medium-Term Development Plan (Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Menengah Nasional [RPJMN]) 2025–2029, and ultimately contribute to the National Long-Term Development Plan (Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Panjang [RPJP]) 2025–2045.

titles: Protection and Promotion of Human Rights
descriptions: To advance the promotion of a safe and enabling environment for human rights through youth empowerment and participation.

titles: Strengthening Democratic Resilience
descriptions: To strengthen democratic resilience by increasing political participation in communities and incubating youth movements and organisations into emerging parties with democratic foundations.

titles: Supporting Environmental Human Rights Defenders
descriptions: To promote a safe and enabling environmental for environmental human rights defenders in which their rights are protected and respected by (1) increasing public awareness on the important contributions of environmental human rights defenders and (2) improve defenders’ capacities in engaging in the 2025 Midterm Elections.

titles: Data Analytics in Politics

titles: Safety Conference for Women Journalists: Gendered Experiences in Election Coverage
descriptions: Specialised training to equip women journalists with knowledge and skills to navigate the specific risks they face, including gender-based online and offline harassment, while ensuring their accurate, impartial and secure coverage of electoral processes.

titles: The path to autonomy: socioeconomic empowerment of disabled women in Niamey via vocation and digital entrepreneurship training.
descriptions:
The project specifically aims to strengthen the skills of women with disabilities in Niamey on digital technology, women's entrepreneurship and sewing, thus promoting their socio-economic inclusion.
To achieve these objectives, various activities are planned.
Firstly, the organisation of a kick-off workshop followed by two specific training sessions on the rights of persons with disabilities to raise awareness and prepare the participants for the continuation of the project (Activity 1).This will be followed by eight in-depth training sessions on entrepreneurship, digital marketing and the use of smartphones, providing beneficiaries with new skills (Activity 2). At the same time, 27 practical training sessions in women's sewing will be organized followed by the provision of sewing machines to strengthen their professional skills (Activity 3).
In addition, ten networking and networking sessions with institutions will be organised to open up new opportunities for beneficiaries (Activity 4). Finally, the organisation of the fair for women entrepreneurs with disabilities will promote and strengthen the visibility of their activities (Activity 5).
The expected outputs will be: 30 women with disabilities trained in their rights, digital technology and entrepreneurship; and know how to use social networks; 30 others trained in sewing and the provision of sewing machines to their groups (10 groups). These products will contribute directly to the achievement of the project's objectives, enabling the empowerment, promotion of activities and socio-economic inclusion of beneficiaries.

titles: Empowering rural women in the production, processing and marketing of local products.
descriptions:
In Niger, the situation of rural women is extremely worrying. Illiterate, and unaware of their rights and those of their children, they are at the mercy of poverty and remain subject to numerous socio-cultural discriminations. Those that have been able to integrate into the agri-food production sectors remain vulnerable due to multiple factors, including a lack of knowledge of certain simple principles likely to secure their investment and increase its value. Community-based organisations such as Transform Niger can play a key role in building the capacity of rural women. This project, submitted by the NGO Transform Niger, will contribute to solving a major problem of socio-economic vulnerability of women members of women's groups in the localities of Kobi and Louma through specific capacity-building measures including training in market gardening, learning dyeing and manual embroidery. Thanks to your support, Transform Niger will realize its social vision of responsibility by working to empower women and girls, reduce inequalities and fight against gender-based violence.

titles: Supporting enhanced transparency in extractive industries gopvernance and promoting civic space through PWYP and the EITI.
descriptions:
