To achieve this overall objective and the specific objectives of this project, ROTAB intends to: Educate, raise awareness and inform the public, local communities and people with disabilities on their rights in relation to mining and oil exploitation through the 2023 EITI standard (requirement N°2). Indeed, it is time to capitalize on experiences in the use of fees retroceded to municipalities through the collection of data from 2018-2023. For the proper participation of civil society actors who sit in the GMC EITI will strengthen their capacities on PWYP's Vision 2025 and other transparency standards in Niger. A follow-up plan for the continuous recommendations in the Niger EITI reports will be developed and executed. 

This project will be implemented in accordance with the principles of results-based management and the participatory approach with the beneficiaries as well as the use of new technology and digital technology through platforms.

titles: Dark Histories / Bright Futures – Restorative Approaches to Modernist Heritage
descriptions: The purpose of this project is to support the Asmara Heritage Project in safeguarding Eritrea’s unique modernist heritage and to provide an international exemplar of how cultural heritage, irrespective of its provenance, is an effective tool for positive long-term change. Asmara’s modernist heritage is a product not only of coloniality, but also of fascism and protracted global and intra-African power struggles throughout the 20th century. Despite this difficult and often dark history, the city was inscribed on the United Nations Educational Scientific Cultural Organisation  World Heritage List in 2017 as Africa’s first, and still only, modern site on the World Heritage List.

titles: Supporting the Ministry of Education officials participate in Education World Forum EWF24
descriptions: As part of the Embassy’s objectives to improve bilateral relations and boost the capacity of the Ministry of Education Eritrea, British Embassy in Asmara is facilitating and supporting travel of the Ministry's officials, including the Acting Minister, who are invited by Secretary of State for Education to participate in The Education World Forum 2024. This will enable the Minister and his team to travel the UK and meet key UK-Education interlocutors to improve the country’s education system. The Minister will also meet UK officials in a brief exchange, demonstrating the UK’s value in the relationship with the Government of Eritrea.

titles: Digitization of Seed Potato Information system
descriptions: This project is part of the larger initiative at national level to create a sustainable framework that supports adaptive capacities within Eritrea’s agriculture sector by improving information flow and capacity building of farmers through digital channels. It also complements the joint Vita Impact /Ministry of Agriculture / European Union project “Multi-Stakeholder Coordination and Community Based Organisation Harnessing for Improved Potato Seed Systems and Value Chains that will be implemented over the coming three years. At a cost of £30,000.00, this micro-project will be implemented over a period of three months.

titles: HEAD OUT TOGETHER: a hip surgery training action
descriptions: The overall objective of the project is to improve the quality of public health services in Eritrea, specifically in the field of Paediatric Orthopaedics, by providing expertise to enable healthcare staff to make accurate early diagnoses to reduce the impact of DDH (Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip) in Eritrean infants and children. This will lead to the prevention of deformities caused by undiagnosed hip dysplasia and, consequently, facilitate the treatment of this condition at all stages.

titles: Integrated Sustainable Development in Dairy, Nursery and Water Conservation in Zoba Maakel and Debub
descriptions: This project has 4 components each wielding sustainability after its completion. First is to secure year-round availability of water by renovating a micro-dam in Halhale sub-zoba of the Debub Region. This small dam has been playing a significant role in improving the water table level of the wells around the area and securing year-round availability of water for research projects including horticulture, agronomy and livestock (forage). The project also aims to support a nursery which has been preparing over half a million seedlings in Bet Ghergish Seedling centre. The water supply system has been having challenges. The submersible pump has been out of use and needs urgent attention. The third component of the project is to support the Dairy production and research centre at Halhale, Zoba Debub. The procurement of concentrate feed for 6 months and the procurement of irrigation materials for forage production will improve milk production. Training in tissue culture research for is the fourth component of the project. Relatively this area of research is at its infant stage. With the existing facilities and staff, the research unit is producing some clean and healthy planting materials such as potatoes, bananas, and date palms.

titles: Strengthening Community-Based Partnerships and Building Skills and Capabilities for Women and Girls in Lesotho
descriptions: Supporting communities to tackle Gender Based Violence and to provide inclusive skills development for women and girls in areas of Lesotho undergoing rapid economic transformation as a result of the expansion of the renewable energy sector.

titles: Supporting inclusive education opportunities for children with disabilities in Lesotho
descriptions: To provide children with disabilities in Lesotho with the support and opportunities they need to help them fulfil their potential, physically, intellectually, and socially. POP Lesotho will aim to build on its achievements, increase the capacity of stakeholders to assess and provide Assistive Technology (AT) and support infrastructure and training facilities for children with cerebral palsy.

titles: Providing skills training, education, and opportunities for Child-Headed Households in Lesotho
descriptions: Delivering practical skills and supplementing education for Child-Headed Households in Lesotho as well as generating access to opportunities.  The project will focus on the Maseru and Berea districts of Lesotho to provide a broad spectrum of opportunities and skills including entrepreneurialism that will facilitate access to markets for significantly disadvantaged young people and their guardians.

titles: Building the evidence base to support governance reform in Lesotho
descriptions: The project will establish means to collate and preserve the existing evidence base of information in Lesotho that can be used to drive decision-making on necessary governance reforms including through the National Reforms process.

titles: Providing access to skills training and mental health expertise for young people in a rural area of Lesotho.
descriptions: Lesotho has the highest suicide rate in the world.  Most people in the country lack access to mental health support.  The project will offer access to mental health expertise and life skills training for young people in Matsieng in order to offer pathways to opportunities and to reduce the risks of negative health outcomes.

titles: Supporting health systems strengthening for palliative care in Lesotho through the development of a best practice methodology
descriptions: Developing a best practice methodology for palliative care in Lesotho through engaging and consulting stakeholders in the healthcare sector.  Lesotho currently lacks meaningful palliative care systems.  This project will help to embed good practices and approaches in advance of finalisation of the first dedicated palliative care centre in the country.

titles: Supporting local solutions to address climate change impacts in the construction sector in Lesotho
descriptions: The project will bring together organisations in Lesotho to generate alternative locally-sourced materials and techniques to reduce the impact of polluting materials in the construction sector.  The project will also address some of the regulatory changes needed to deliver more ambitious climate-resilient approaches in the construction sector in Lesotho.

titles: Facilitating access to essential services for survivors of Gender Based Violence in Lesotho
descriptions: The project will provide outreach in most of the districts of Lesotho in order to bring services for survivors of Gender Based Violence to the places where they live.  It will also sensitise survivors to the availability of those services as well as offering practical lessons and guidance by experts.  Most services are centred on the capital, Maseru.  The project will make expert service provision more visible and available around the rest of Lesotho, a country where around 80% of women report having been subjected to Gender Based Violence.

titles: Fourth Replenishment of the Multilateral Investment Fund - Inter-American Development Bank
descriptions:
This is the UK’s fourth replenishment to the Multilateral Investment Fund (MIF IV, known as IDB Lab), the innovation and venture capital arm of the Inter-American Development Bank Group (IDBG), supporting early-stage private sector innovation across Latin America and the Caribbean through to 2031. IDB Lab plays a unique role among multilateral development banks, enabling technology and entrepreneurship for poor and vulnerable populations, with a sharpened strategic focus on climate action, gender equality, and Caribbean small island developing states (SIDS). The business case notes that MIF IV will finance 80 operations per year, deploying $1.2 billion and reaching an estimated 47 million people directly. This is a 33% increase in reach per dollar compared to the previous replenishment. The replenishment raises climate finance targets to 40%, with 70% of projects supporting gender equality and 25% promoting diversity. At least 60% of operations will directly support the poor and vulnerable, and 17% of funding will go to Small and Island Countries, reflecting the UK’s priorities in the region.

The UK’s recommended contribution (up to US$3m, not exceeding a 1% burden share) will be matched 1:1 by IDB income and will mobilise further third-party resources, supporting a more sustainable funding model and reducing reliance on donor funds. IDB Lab’s strengthened results framework will track innovation, scalability, and outcomes, including reach, depth, and value of impact. The UK’s negotiating objectives have been met, with greater financial stability, increased strategic focus, and additional support for the Caribbean. This investment aligns with UK priorities on poverty eradication, climate resilience, gender and social inclusion, and strengthens UK influence in shaping innovation and development outcomes in the region, while generating lessons for the wider global financial system.

titles: Building State Effectiveness through Problem-Driven Iterative Adaptation and Institutional and Policy Engagement through TAF
descriptions: The project aims to support the improvement of state effectiveness in Bangladesh to reduce poverty, improve service delivery and increase growth with the secondary benefit of increased trade with the UK and growth in the UK

titles: Stakeholder Engagement - Review of the Current Landscape and Future Prospects of Engineering Biology in Malaysia and Thailand
descriptions: The overarching Project aims to gain insights and recommendations on the current landscape, as well as forward-looking opportunities (foresight) for Malaysia and Thailand government as well as all stakeholders working towards the development and implementation of engineering biology systems, as well as for the interested UK stakeholders. Specifically for this stakeholder engagement activity, we will host a session in the Thailand’s Synbio Consortium Meeting on 11 November 2024. As the Meeting will convene already key EngBio stakeholders (policy-makers such as the Science Policy Council, academia, and industries) in Thailand, this presents a great opportunity for Thailand Academy of Science and Technology to not only outline the preliminary study of Thailand EngBio landscape, but also to consult with all relevant stakeholders during the meeting, and to conduct foresight study in one go. The Project will also help to provide insights into specific areas with opportunities for the UK to further engage, both on business and research side.

titles: Generating Critical Mass and Public Awareness about the Southern Thai Peace Process
descriptions: To support The Asia Foundation's (the Foundation's) work on capacity building for Thai journalists covering the conflict in the far South and to generate greater public understanding of the findings and recommendations from the Parliament Ad Hoc Committee tasked with studying the Southern Thai peace process. The project aims to contribute to civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution, as well as media and free flow of information.

titles: Professional Development Course on Peacebuilding for Civil Servants in Southern Thailand
descriptions: The implementing partner, Institute for Peace Studies (IPS), will be working with representatives of the Southern Border Provinces Administration Centre (SBPAC), a key government centre for administrating the conflict affected provinces, to create a tailored-made professional development peace training programmes for the responsible authorities on  peace dialogue and mediation in Thailand's Southernmost region. The project will be engaging the Royal Thai Police and other civilian agencies based in the South to gauge their interest in joining the training program.  As Thailand is gradually returning to civilian rule after a decade of military domination in Thai politics, the team believes that it is important to capacitate civilian agencies, which are supposed to play central roles in conflict resolution in the Deep South.

titles: The visit of new DOC inspectors to the UK to shadow prison inspection
descriptions: New inspectors of Thai Department of Corrections (DOC) have an opportunity to shadow His Majesty’s Inspectorate of Prisons (HMIP) and witness how prison inspection is conducted in the UK. This will give them a clearer picture which may lead to a concrete change to Thai prison inspection mechanism. Ultimate goal is to strengthen Thai prison inspection to highlight where standards are not being met and conditions need to improve so that the risk to detained BNs and other nationalities can be reduced.

titles: Strengthening UK-Thailand Partnerships: Advancing Democracy, Human Rights, and Sustainable Trade and Economic Development
descriptions: The aim of the project is to meet with government officials, parliamentarians and civil society organisations to encourage constitutional reform, support greater political participation, and defend human rights, ultimately creating a more stable democratic government that can drive greater trade and sustainable growth between the UK and Thailand.

titles: UK/RTP Custody and Detention Project (Phase 4)
descriptions: The project aims to improve police detention policy and practice in Thailand. Overall, improved custody and detention process will increase good practice, consistency and transparency of a suspect’s detention. Any BNs subject to arrest will be handled properly at the pilot police station and in potential roll-out.

titles: Gen AI for Gen Z: Inspiring new generation of AI creators
descriptions: Despite growing excitement about AI, Cambodia faces low understanding and experience in applying these powerful tools. The need to address biases and ethical AI use early is crucial for responsible applications. Currently, only 10% of Cambodian students choose IT fields, creating a significant gap in the country's AI readiness."GenAI for Gen Z" is a unique educational program designed to target Cambodian youth, ensuring at least 50% female participation. This project will introduce the transformative power of Generative AI, sparking a shift within Cambodian students. By bringing diverse genders together, we foster open discussions and understanding. We specifically target students from social and humanitarian sciences—particularly women—to inspire them with AI's potential, unleashing new possibilities for collaboration and creative applications.As a leader in innovation and STEM support, the UK can play a pivotal role in fostering Cambodia's AI future. Funding this project helps bridge a knowledge gap, promotes inclusivity and responsible AI development, empowers underrepresented students, and inspires a new generation of tech creators in Cambodia. This investment aligns directly with the UK's goals of promoting technological leadership and global collaboration, as well as the principles laid out in the Bletchley Declaration for fostering public trust and confidence in AI systems.

titles: Scholarship Program for Primary Education

By integrating the families into our Income Generation Program, as into community Savings Groups and Farmer Field Schools, we hope to sustain the family's financial stability, hence supporting the students' long-term education. titles: Prev3C – Prevention of Cervical Cancer in Cambodia

The SHERCAN project aims to increase awareness of CC and available services, and strengthen the health system to provide CC prevention services. titles: One drop one hope: Drip Irrigation in Southern Angola
descriptions: The project plans to implement drip irrigation systems in rural communities in Cunene, Huila and Namibe who rely on small scale farming and are constantly affected by seasonal draught in Angola. Through a study-based data collection, we will implement cost effetely, eco-friendly and efficient method of watering crops, providing more uniform, timely and precise application of water. The project involves constructing a network of drip irrigation tape which delivers water to the base of the plants, either on the soil surface or underneath, directly on the root zone. The outcome of this project is a more rapid growth and earlier harvest, higher quality crops at higher yields as well as cost saving associated with greatly reduced water usage in period of drought, especially this year with the impact of El Nino. Emphasis will be given to women and young girls who are household heads and have farming as a source for food security and living income for their families. The purpose of this project is to provide a sustainable and practical long-term solution to combat the impact of seasonal drought in the south of Angola on food security and farming.

titles: Contribution to the Basket Fund of the MAPP/OAS in Colombia
descriptions: The MAPP/OAS in Colombia seeks to support the government and its citizens in achieving comprehensive and sustainable peace with all armed groups across the national territory. As a strategic partner, the Mission offers an innovative and adaptable model of international cooperation, built on over two decades of experience, territorial presence, and continuous engagement with stakeholders. This enables it to provide timely and context-sensitive recommendations to the Colombian State, addressing both achievements and ongoing challenges in peace consolidation. The 2025–2027 Institutional Strategic Plan is based on process and results-oriented management, aligning three strategic objectives with twelve mission and support processes. Following a detailed analysis of strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats, MAPP/OAS reaffirmed the relevance of its flexible mandate, especially in regions most affected by conflict. In 2025/26, the Mission will play a key role in peace dialogues, strengthen institutions through knowledge sharing, and promote environmental governance and community participation. Its priorities include consolidating its support model, positioning its expertise for policy advocacy, contributing to environmental protection in conflict zones, and advancing gender and women’s rights agendas. Capacity building for dialogue and conflict transformation remains central, particularly for actors in socio-environmental conflicts and peace processes. The Mission will continue to provide analysis and recommendations on security, community impacts, and environmental issues, including the use of anti-personnel mines and contamination of water sources. Each year, MAPP/OAS adjusts its focus based on contextual analysis. In 2025, it will prioritise peace dialogues, victims’ rights, environmental and civilian impacts, safety conditions, implementation of the Final Peace Agreement, community engagement, transitional justice, and capacity building for peace.

titles: Strategies for the implementation of the 2016 Peace Agreement, territorial transformation and peace consolidation

titles: Strengthening territorial capacities for the implementation of the Women, Peace and Security agenda in Colombia.

This will contribute to a transformative shift in how public institutions and feminist movements co-lead the Women, Peace and Security agenda, ensuring its integration into territorial realities, institutional practices, legal frameworks, and international 
advocacy spaces.

titles: Strengthen institutional & community capacities to drive peacebuildin & access to justice in conflict-affected areas in Colombia
descriptions: The main activities of the programme include strengthening institutional and community capacities to effectively drive peacebuilding processes in territories affected by armed conflict. This will be achieved through the implementation of specific protection systems for community leaders and human rights defenders, and by ensuring access to justice for the victims of the conflict. Additionally, the programme will support the creation and development of social cohesion and community development initiatives, promoting the active participation of local communities in rebuilding the social fabric and consolidating peace in their territories. These activities are designed to address both immediate needs and structural challenges, ensuring a sustainable and lasting impact in the affected areas.

titles: Supporting communities, victims, and human rights defenders in preventing violence and insecurity, and ensuring their inclusion.

titles: Empowering Voices: Tackling Political Violence Against Women Leaders and political candidates in Colombia’s Pre-Election Period
descriptions: The purpose of the project is to strengthen protection mechanisms for addressing the risks of political violence faced by women's human rights defenders and candidates during the 2025-2026 electoral cycle in Colombia.

titles: Strengthening prosecutorial methodology to investigate and dismantle organised criminal networks in Colombia (SPMOC)
descriptions:
This project will strengthen the Prosecutor’s Office capacity to dismantle organised criminal networks by developing, validating, and beginning institutional adoption of a unified methodology to investigate and prosecute these structures as integrated criminal systems. The project will deliver: (1) a methodological and operational framework that sets principles, structured prosecutorial processes, analytical criteria, and practical tools; and (2) a specialised module for illicit economies linked to fuel-station networks, including typologies, risk indicators, territorial and financial linkages, and evidentiary routes.
Activities include a diagnostic based on case analysis and practitioner consultations, a co-design workshop with territorial and central teams, iterative drafting and refinement of both components, and pilot use in selected units supported by case-based exercises. These activities will produce operational guidance and a practical adoption roadmap that supports internal uptake beyond the project period.
This system-focused approach improves strategic case design, strengthens analytical-investigative coordination, and enhances the State's ability to weaken criminal structures over time. UK support ensures methodological rigor, continuity with previous engagement, and independent quality assurance through strategic oversight, technical review, and financial support. At the same time, this methodological approach is aimed at reducing crime by enabling prosecutors to map and dismantle entire criminal networks rather than isolated nodes, preventing their regeneration.

titles: Contribution to the United Nations Post-conflict Multi-donor Trust Fund in Colombia
descriptions:
The Trust Fund for Sustaining Peace in Colombia supports coordinated responses for stabilization and peacebuilding. Aligned with CONPES 3850 guidelines, the Trust Fund finances thematic priorities that provide transparent, effective, and results-based solutions to immediate and medium-term post-conflict priorities in Colombia.

To ensure national ownership and improved coordination, the United Nations works with the Government of Colombia to mobilize funds for the coordination of interventions that support the national Rapid Response Strategy, early roll-out and scaling-up of agreements that cater to vulnerable communities, and address drivers of conflict as prioritized by national authorities.

The Trust Fund is closely aligned with the national stabilization strategy for Colombia. Strategic objectives support initiatives that:
 
Increase trust between local communities and authorities, strengthen rule of law and institutional mechanisms, and boost democratic participation in peace processes.

Increase community confidence in peace processes and their transformative potential, particularly for survivors of violence and communities of territories affected by armed conflict.

Avoid and/or mitigate drivers of crime and violence (associated with armed conflict), and reduce the effects of coercion and violence (real and perceived).

Manage community and/or social conflict through early interventions that resolve or transform community demands into dialogue processes and prevent social rifts from expanding.

Achieve early security, justice, and development wins that threaten to undermine peace processes and help stakeholders manage challenges.

titles: Supporting Commonwealth Small States and Least Developed Countries Effective Engagement in the Fields of Human Rights and Trade
descriptions:
Human rights: 
The project’s purpose is to enhance the capacity of Commonwealth Small States and Least Developed Countries (LDCs) to engage effectively with the UN human rights mechanisms, including the Human Rights Council (HRC), Universal Periodic Review (UPR) mechanism and Treaty Bodies (TBs) and to that end, strengthen their national frameworks. Effective member state engagement with UN human rights mechanisms will lead to their enhanced voice and increased visibility. It will enable them to further strengthen their overall partnership with these mechanisms, and benefit from constructive recommendations to improve conditions at the national level for increased human rights promotion and protection. Strengthened national frameworks will provide the necessary policy frameworks and a platform to monitor and report on the implementation of UN recommendations at the national level.   

Trade: 
The project’s purpose is to strengthen the capacity of Commonwealth Small States (CSS) to engage more effectively in negotiations on existing and new and emerging trade issues at the WTO and facilitate their fuller integration and participation in the multilateral trading system. Small States rely heavily on international trade as a driver of growth and development, and deeper integration into the multilateral trading system will help expand trade and investment opportunities, including within the Commonwealth. Moreover, given their heightened vulnerability to climate change and natural disasters, trade can serve as a vital tool for recovery and building long-term resilience.

titles: Strengthening Commonwealth Member Countries to Access Climate Finance
descriptions:
To advance equitable and inclusive climate action in small and other vulnerable Commonwealth states, through enhanced access to international climate finance and strengthened technical, human and institutional capacity. 

Context and Need for the Project
In no more than 200 words, provide the background and context to the issues this project will address and why the UK should fund this project




 
The Commonwealth Climate Change Programme focuses on strengthening the resilience of Commonwealth countries to the impacts of climate change. It provides technical assistance and capacity development support to member countries to access climate finance for climate mitigation and adaptation through the Commonwealth Climate Finance Access Hub (CCFAH). It supports integrated action on the three Rio Conventions through the implementation of the Living Lands Charter. As of March 2025, CCFAH has supported 21 countries in Africa, Indo-Pacific, and the Caribbean, securing approximately USD 473.55 million for various climate projects and training about 3,305 government officials through 152 capacity-building initiatives.

This funding from the FCDO, building on previous support including in FY24-25, will be used to cover the costs and expenses for Commonwealth National Climate Finance Adviser (CNCFA) in Maldives, Namibia and Mauritius, and the Commonwealth Regional Climate Finance Adviser (CRCFA) in the Caribbean region – nations and a region that are highly vulnerable to climate change. 

The UK’s renewed commitment to climate leadership, exemplified by its ambitious 81% emissions reduction target by 2035, positions it as a trusted partner and climate leader, a reputation reinforced by this funding which will facilitate low-carbon transitions and de-risk investments in the long run. Strengthening climate adaptation in the Caribbean (a key Commonwealth trade partner) safeguards UK-linked industries like agriculture and tourism from climate disruptions.

descriptions: This project supports the UK’s international development objectives by enabling responsible use of emerging technologies to improve the lives of people in poverty. It helps FCDO staff and partners design, test, and scale innovative solutions to global challenges such as climate change, disability inclusion, and access to essential services. Activities include real-world experimentation, capacity building, and research to strengthen local ecosystems and promote equitable technology adoption. The project aims to benefit 8 million people in developing countries and leverages £5 million in co-funding to support early-stage ideas. All activities align with the Sustainable Development Goals and promote inclusive, ethical, and locally relevant innovation. The project also contributes to strengthening FCDO’s internal innovation capacity and supports the Foreign Secretary’s ambition to modernise development through technology.

titles: Pride Receptions to mark Pride Month
descriptions:
This project aims to advance the rights and visibility of the LGBTIQ+ community in Vietnam by hosting two high-profile Pride events at the British Embassy in Hanoi and the British Consulate General in Ho Chi Minh City. By leveraging the UK’s strong reputation as an advocate for LGBTIQ+ rights, the events will raise awareness of LGBTIQ+ issues, foster allyship, and reinforce the importance of protecting civic space. 

Activities such as film screening and panel/group conversations with community activists will highlight the lived realities of LGBTIQ+ people in Vietnam, creating a platform for shared experiences and collective reflection on the country’s evolving social landscape, including public discussion around the draft same-sex marriage law. The evening receptions will further these outputs by celebrating diversity through cultural performances, mobilising allies, and strengthening collaboration with Hanoi Pride, VietPride, and partner organisations. 

These outputs serve the project’s broader purpose: to sustain and empower networks of activists, organisations, and allies in a challenging environment. By keeping civic space open, nurturing dialogue, and connecting communities with supportive partners, the project helps maintain momentum for future progress and positions activists to engage more effectively when conditions allow.

titles: Digital Transformation of Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) Reporting and Pharmacovigilance System in Viet Nam
descriptions:
This project will deliver core modules of a secure digital platform for ADR reporting and pharmacovigilance in Viet Nam, to the point of initial testing and piloting. Through four integrated Activities, the project will map current regulatory processes, provide pharmacovigilance advisory support, develop and deploy core modules of a modern ADR system, and build local capacity to use it. 

First, the ADR Centre’s workflows and requirements will be analysed in detail, producing process maps and technical specifications for optimal system design. Next, priority regulatory processes and data flows interfacing with pharmacovigilance will be documented, ensuring the new system fits into broader medicines regulation. Based on these designs, an E2B(R3)-standards-compliant ADR digital system will be developed. Existing ADR data will be standardised and migrated. Necessary hardware will be procured. The system will be tested and piloted, and initial training provided to pharmacovigilance staff. Pharmacovigilance technical advice will be provided, including in relation to use of high-quality ADR data in HTA.

These Outputs will directly achieve the project Purpose by improving data timeliness and quality, creating real-world impact as regulators can more quickly identify safety problems, more efficiently engage industry, and protect patients. Importantly, the detailed process mapping will guide future investments in digitalising Viet Nam’s medicine regulatory system, making this a catalytic project for larger-scale innovation.

agency: Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy
titles: Regionalism in East Africa c. 1900 to the present
descriptions: This project will undertake the first comprehensive historical study of regionalism in East Africa in the twentieth century. Ideas about formal political and economic integration among the various territories of East Africa have a deep history in the region, dating back to the colonial period, and currently manifested in the institutions of the (second) East African Community, an intergovernmental organisation comprised of six eastern African states: Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi and South Sudan. Partly owing to this deep and continuing history, East African regionalism has often been seen as a beacon of effective regional integration in Africa, and assertions of a powerful sense of common regional identity - even destiny - have been an important part of the official rhetoric of the EAC over several decades. But the extent to which regional integration has delivered positive public outcomes or alternatively simply served the interests of a small regional elite in East Africa remains hotly contested (reflecting broader global debates on this issue). This project will engage this central question within both a regional and global setting, examining the origins, character and outcomes of regional integration initiatives as the product both of East African internal dynamics as well as of interlinked global structures and processes (colonialism, decolonisation, global regionalisms, and neo-liberalism). In so doing it will fill a major lacunae in the current scholarly literature on the history and politics of East Africa, moving beyond methodological nationalism to write a history of attempts at building region alongside nation. More broadly, the persistence of regionalism as a political and economic phenomenon in East Africa over time also makes the region an excellent case for examining and historicising wider debates around regionalism in Africa and the world. This project, which builds on a successfully completed pilot study (British Academy funded - regional integration in 1960s-70s East Africa) brings together a team of historians and political scientists to examine a) the colonial origins of integration projects - ideas of 'closer union' and federation that were debated amongst settlers and colonial officials in British East Africa during the first half of the twentieth century, alongside the establishment of regional institutions by the British b) ideas of federation and 'community' that emerged among nationalists and East African publics in the years of decolonisation and independence, c) the establishment and collapse of the first East African Community between 1965 and 1977 d) the revival and expansion of the East African Community from the 1990s to the present. Throughout we will focus on key themes including a) the shifting intellectual content of regionalist visions (pan-Africanism; federalism; state-led developmentalism; neo-liberalism) b) the politics of integration in the context of intra-regional relations more broadly c) the (uneven) economic impact of regional integration d) the role of external actors in shaping regional integration projects, and the role of local elite agency in mediating or transforming external interventions e) continuities and changes in the above themes over time. The research will utilise archival documentation, press material, official reports and interviews with figures involved in regional integration to produce academic and non-academic outputs that will make a major contribution to academic debate on global regionalisms and to policy discussions on the future of regional integration in East Africa.

agency: Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy
titles: Values-based Climate Change Risk Assessment: Piloting the Climate Vulnerability Index for Cultural Heritage in Africa [Highlight Notice]
descriptions: Climate change poses an existential threat to all humanity. Understanding this change and adapting to it has become the greatest challenge of our time. From rising sea-levels, more extreme weather events and aridification, the extensive impacts of climate are evident at heritage sites globally and the pace of this change is startling. In most parts of the world the rate of loss is exceeding adaptive capacity and this deficit is only getting worse, especially in the global south. Decisions on conservation and preservation begin with a detailed understanding of a place's vulnerability. The choices made will directly impact that ability to effectively integrate the goals of safeguarding cultural heritage, adapting and mitigating climate change, and driving sustainable development. Previous assessment methodologies must be revised to accurately evaluate the vulnerability of cultural heritage sites and their associated communities in the face of a changing climate. There is an urgent need to develop community-based, quick (and yet effective) new techniques and methodologies, and these must be scalable globally. The CVI Africa Project seeks to address this need. The proposed research project centres on training heritage professionals through piloting a new, protype heritage management methodology known as the Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI) in Africa. CVI provides an assessment of the physical and ecological impacts of current and projected climate change on the heritage values of sites and also provides a high-level assessment of the economic, social and cultural consequences of climate change for the site and the associated community. The Project is designed both to adapt existing methodology to the African cultural context and also draw on African expertise to inform refinements in the general CVI methodology. The CVI Africa project will provide foundational training in vulnerability assessment using the CVI method to train six heritage professionals from low and middle income African countries. It will utilise UK and international expertise to develop and deliver online, transferrable and scalable training resources to training participants. The project will culminate in two workshops in Nigeria (Sukur Cultural Landscape) and Tanzania (The Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Songo Mnara) which are impacted by climate change. These workshops will include the training participants, local and national experts and stakeholders, and international partners and will culminate in a publicly available and locally published report. The project will also foster new relationships and encourage knowledge exchange by bringing together collaborators from many organisations and working with new and existing members of the Climate Heritage Network (CHN), a network of arts, culture and heritage organisations committed to aiding their communities in tackling climate change and achieving the ambitions of the Paris Agreement. These include lead investigators from Queen's University Belfast, Historic Environment Scotland, the University of Highlands and Islands and the African World Heritage Fund. Local partner organisations include the Tanzanian Ministry of Natural Resources and Tourism and the Nigerian National Commission for Museums and Monuments. Other international partner organisations include the International Committee on Monuments and Sites (ICOMOS), Historic England, the International National Trust Organisation (INTO) and the Union of Concerned Scientists who will all play roles in project training and/ or workshop participation. Finally, the project will work with the UK Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) and other similar projects to develop a longer term and sustainable Overseas Development Assistance (ODA) funded workstream, to respond effectively to climate change impacts on cultural heritage focused on developing countries.
